transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-22
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~47 minutes
Location: Zoom (recording)
Attendees: Alyssa Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Dara Nguyen (Redwood CSM); Tom Reyes (NovusHealth CTO), Priya Desai (ML), Evan Brooks (Product), Sofia Martinez (Security), Liam O'Connor (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Redwood went over latest pilot results (week 2), focusing on model selection and the idea of locking a model version for the remainder of the pilot to avoid regressions. Discussed p95/p99 latency spikes after quantization change, cost tradeoffs between hosted vs dedicated, and fallback/rollback strategies for canary rollouts. Action items: send updated SOW, share trimmed benchmark, customer to validate eval set.

Topics: model selection, version pinning, rollback/fallback policy, latency vs cost, KV cache behavior, quantization artifacts, canary rollout plan, security/egress constraints.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alyssa: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call—Redwood on my side, Marcus and Dara. NovusHealth, we have Tom, Priya, Evan, Sofia, Liam. Can you all hear me okay?
[00:08] Tom: Yep, loud and clear.
[00:10] Priya: Good here.
[00:12] Alyssa: Cool. Today we want to focus on week two pilot results and then lock down a model version for week three — and also go through fallback rules. Marcus, want to kick off with the performance highlights?
[00:25] Marcus: Sure. I pulled the trimmed benchmarks — I sent a link in the chat, it's the reduced sheet: "pilot-benchmarks-week2-trimmed.xlsx". High level: hosted baseline (redwood-host-small) with model v1.3 quantized int8 shows p50 ~ 110ms per token, p95 ~ 480ms, p99 ~ 920ms on your workload samples. Dedicated instance with the same model and config hits p50 ~ 90ms, p95 ~ 320ms, p99 ~ 560ms. So dedicated narrows tail latency a lot.
[01:02] Evan: I noticed cost went up slightly when we enabled prefix caching — shouldn't caching reduce tokens and cost?
[01:10] Marcus: Good question. Caching reduces compute per request, but the way we configured it initially you had frequent short sessions which didn't hit the cache much; after enabling eager cache persistence the effective token compute dropped, but the benchmark we sent includes a mix where cache warmed and cold starts still exist. We can run a cache-warm-only slice.
[01:30] Priya: On the p99 numbers, we saw some weird spikes after you switched the quantization profile Wednesday night. Is that expected? The outputs had occasional hallucination-like tokens too.
[01:40] Marcus: Right, so the int8 quant profile we used trades off a smidge of perplexity for speed. Most of the time it's fine, but we did observe occasional degenerate completions on long-context prompts — that's probably due to a precision dropout in a small submodule. We flagged it and rolled back the profile on Friday night for the continuous runs. The spike you saw is from the interim runs.
[02:05] Tom: Can we pin to the older model build then? We'd rather have consistent quality for demos.
[02:10] Alyssa: Absolutely. That's what this sync is for — proposing a model-lockdown for the rest of the pilot so the customer sees stable outputs while we can experiment in a separate branch. We usually support version pinning at the route level. Marcus, what's the easiest way for NovusHealth to pin?
[02:25] Marcus: Two options: 1) pin the exact model artifact name (e.g., redwood-model-llamax:v1.2.4) at the API route so all traffic uses that binary, or 2) pin to a model family with an explicit rollout policy that sets an allowlist of versions and disables auto-upgrades. For pilot stability I'd recommend option 1 — lock to v1.2.4. That prevents drift.
[02:50] Priya: If we pin to v1.2.4, can we still use the dedicated hosts we tested?
[02:56] Marcus: Yes — dedicated pools are agnostic to model version. We can schedule the pinned version on your reserved pool. The only gotcha is if you later want a quantized variant (e.g., the int8 speedup) we'd need to build and validated that variant and then change the route config.
[03:14] Sofia: From security we'll want an audit trail of any change — who flips a pin, timestamp, and a diffable config. Is that in your console?
[03:22] Dara: Yes — the Redwood Console logs route config changes and we can export audit entries. We also support SAML SSO and RBAC so only authorized project admins can change pins. We can throw a sample audit export to you.
[03:34] Sofia: Great, please send that.
[03:36] [04:00] Marcus: Back to fallback/rollback—recommendation is to configure a two-tier fallback: primary pinned model (v1.2.4), secondary fallback to a compatible small-family model (e.g., redwood-llama-mini:v0.9) only for short-circuits when the primary exceeds latency or error thresholds. Then a tertiary route to the hosted best-effort for non-blocking degradation.
[04:22] Liam: How do you enforce that? Like if p95 crosses 600ms we want an automatic failover — can that be automated?
[04:28] Marcus: Yes, we can set route policies with SLO gates: if p95 > 600ms for 5 minutes OR error rate > 2% for 3 minutes, automatically switch traffic to the fallback route. You can also configure a gradual roll-back where 10% shifts every 30s to test the fallback.
[04:45] Priya: Will that break session state / KV cache? We rely on KV cache for context acceleration.
[04:52] Marcus: Good catch — switching to a smaller family won't share token KV cache with the primary. That causes cold-cache overhead and can change latencies. We usually set the fallback to only trigger for idempotent routes (batch jobs or short-turn queries). For stateful chat sessions we recommend a canary or can handle-by-session sticky routing so individual user sessions can be pinned.
[05:15] Evan: So maybe for our demo flows we pin sessions to the primary and don't auto-fail on sessioned endpoints?
[05:20] Alyssa: That sounds reasonable — we can set route-level sticky session rules and separate non-sessioned endpoints for aggressive fallback.
[05:27] Tom: What about rollback safety? If a new model is rolled out and regresses, can we instantly revert?
[05:33] Marcus: Yes — console supports instant rollback to any prior pinned version and also supports running a regression test suite during rollout — you can gate by quality metrics like BLEU/ROUGE/Custom evals. We can add your eval prompts to the gate.
[05:50] Priya: I'll need help integrating our evals. We have about 150 golden prompts and some safety checks.
[05:56] Marcus: Happy to help — send the prompt set; Marcus (SE) will run them against both v1.2.4 and the v1.3 quant profile and send a diff.
[06:06] Alyssa: Note in the chat: Marcus will run evals.
[06:09] [06:30] Marcus: On costs — hosted baseline measured $0.018 per 1k tokens with the current config; dedicated cut that to about $0.012 per 1k tokens due to packing and sustained utilization. Quantization lowered that further theoretically but given quality regressions we pulled it back. If you expect steady traffic, committed dedicated may be cost-effective.
[06:48] Tom: How much commit do we need for Dedicated? We're still in pilot — we don't want a big monthly commit.
[06:55] Alyssa: We have flexible short-term reserved bursts for pilots — e.g., a small reserved pool for the pilot month with burst capacity. I'll include the small dedicated pilot SKU in the SOW.
[07:05] Sofia: Re: compliance — are logs with PII masked? We need assurance on retention and masking rules.
[07:12] Dara: Yes, Redwood supports PII redaction at ingestion and configurable retention windows; we also integrate KMS for customer-managed keys for encryption-at-rest. We'll push the security whitepaper and sample audit exports.
[07:26] Priya: One small nit — yesterday in the sandbox I saw name entity "NovoHealth" instead of "NovusHealth" in a few transcripts; the speech-to-text seems to auto-correct. Not a big deal but FYI.
[07:36] Marcus: Noted — transcription quirks.
[07:38] [08:00] Evan: Back to fallback — what about partial rollbacks? Suppose v1.3 is live, we find a regression in a subset of prompts — can we roll back only for those prompt families?
[08:12] Marcus: You can use route match rules: if the request metadata matches a tag (e.g., prompt-type:doc-summaries) route to pinned version; otherwise use v1.3. That requires tagging at the client side or route pre-processing.
[08:25] Priya: We can add a prompt-type header from our proxy.
[08:28] Marcus: Perfect — that will let you do surgical rollbacks without affecting global traffic.
[08:32] [09:00] Tom: Cool. Let's talk about canary cadence — what's typical for you?
[09:05] Marcus: For production we generally recommend: 1) internal smoke tests, 2) 1% canary for 10 minutes, 3) 10% for 30 minutes (with automatic rollback on regressions), 4) progressive to 50% then 100%. For pilots you can compress that to 1% -> 25% -> 100% with longer evaluation windows if you need.
[09:26] Alyssa: We'll propose a canary plan for the next call.
[09:30] [10:00] Priya: A quick question about the catalog — in your console I saw two similarly named items: redwood-llamax and redwood-llamax-optimized. Which should we prefer?
[10:10] Marcus: The optimized build includes kernel-level heuristics for specific sequence lengths and improved memory layout; it typically reduces p99 on long sequences but can differ on exact token distribution. For now, prefer the non-optimized family for deterministic outputs if you care more about output parity.
[10:29] Priya: Good to know. We'll stick with non-optimized for demos.
[10:34] [11:00] Alyssa: Next, any blockers from NovusHealth side on pinning?
[11:05] Liam: Network limits — our VPC egress to the Redwood dedicated nodes needs an approved rule; otherwise we risk timed-out handshakes during scale events. I'm verifying with infra team but wanted to flag.
[11:17] Dara: We can work with your network team; Marcus can provide example egress IPs and ports.
[11:22] Alyssa: Action: Marcus will provide egress IP list.
[11:25] [12:00] Marcus: Also, we'll include a short doc on sticky sessions and KV cache behavior when switching models — that will help decide fallback policies.
[12:10] Priya: Appreciate that.
[12:12] [13:00] Evan: On the UX, if we pin a model, will logs and tokens show the model version used? We need to tie invoices back to model usage for cost apportioning.
[13:18] Dara: Yes — telemetry includes route-level and model-version breakdowns; you can export token usage per model per day. We'll show a sample export.
[13:26] Tom: Great.
[13:28] [14:00] Alyssa: To recap: 1) We recommend pinning to redwood-model-llamax:v1.2.4 for pilot stability. 2) Configure a two-tier fallback with sticky sessions disabled for non-session endpoints. 3) SE will run your eval set against v1.2.4 and v1.3-quant to produce a diff. 4) Redwood to send updated SOW with small dedicated pilot SKU and pricing delta. 5) Security will receive audit export and whitepaper.
[14:32] Tom: That matches our expectations. Priya, anything to add?
[14:36] Priya: No, just that I'll send the 150 prompt eval set later today.
[14:40] Alyssa: Awesome. Any final questions?
[14:44] Sofia: Please include the retention/PII redaction toggles in the security packet.
[14:49] Alyssa: Will do.
[14:52] [15:00] Marcus: I'll share the trimmed benchmark sheet and the egress IPs before EOD tomorrow.
[15:05] Alyssa: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with SOW and the canary plan.
[15:10] Tom: Thanks all. Bye.

End of transcript.
